info.title: E-Commerce AI Assistant API
info.description:
Order & tracking support assistant API. Customers prove ownership of an order (order number + the email it was placed under) to receive a bearer token scoped to their own email, then use it to list/look up their own orders or chat with an AI assistant that looks up order data on their behalf.

See the repo README for architecture, auth reasoning, rate limits, and everything else not captured by this spec.

servers.description: Same origin as the app - there is no separate API host

tags.name: Orders
tags.description: A customer's own orders - requires a bearer token

tags.name: Chat
tags.description: AI assistant chat - requires a bearer token

bearerAuth.description: Obtained from POST /api/auth/verify. Carries the verified customer's email; expires after 1 hour.

unit_price_cents.description: Product price in cents, before delivery/VAT/voucher.

voucher_cents.description: Discount amount in cents, stored positive and subtracted at display time. 0 when no voucher was applied.

product_icon.description: Identifies which product illustration to render - not derived from product_name.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, or expired bearer token

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded - budget is per authenticated customer for Orders/Chat, per source IP for Auth (see README > Rate limiting)

get.description: Process is up, nothing more - safe for a platform's own restart-on-failure health check. See /health/db for a check that also verifies the database.

Runs a real SELECT 1 against the database - meant for an external uptime monitor, not a platform restart trigger (a transient DB blip shouldn't restart this process, since restarting doesn't fix that).

post.summary: Verify order ownership, receive a bearer token

200.description: Order number + email matched a real order

400.description: orderNumber or email missing from the request body

401.description: No order matches that order number + email pair. Deliberately the same response whether the order number doesn't exist or the email doesn't match it - see README > Authorization.

get.summary: List the authenticated customer's own orders (paginated)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Clamped to [1, 100]; non-integer values are rejected with 400.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque keyset-pagination cursor from a previous response's nextCursor. Omit for the first page.

nextCursor.description: Pass as ?cursor= to fetch the next page; null on the last page.

400.description: limit is not an integer, or cursor doesn't decode to a valid keyset position

get.summary: Fetch a single order by order number

200.description: OK - the order belongs to the authenticated customer

404.description: No such order, or it belongs to a different customer - deliberately the same response either way so this can't be used to enumerate real order numbers (see README > Authorization).

post.summary: Send a conversation turn to the AI assistant
post.description: The assistant looks up the authenticated customer's own order data via tool calls scoped server-side to their email - the model can never be asked to reveal a different customer's data.

messages.description: The full conversation so far, including this turn's new user message. content must be a plain string - see README > Penetration testing for why.

400.description: messages is missing/empty, exceeds 40 entries, or contains an entry with the wrong shape

500.description: The AI provider call failed (e.g. no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY configured) - a generic message, no internal detail
